hints.title: Locate the two stationary points
hints.body: Differentiate to get f′(x)=2x2+4mx=2x(x+2m). Since m>0, the stationary inputs −2m and 0 are distinct.
hints.recap: The stationary heights determine whether a cubic crosses the axis three times.
hints.pitfall: Three distinct roots require more than simply having two stationary points.

recall.reminder: The stationary heights determine whether a cubic crosses the axis three times.

hints.title: Calculate the turning heights
hints.body: Substitute each stationary input into the original cubic and simplify its height. Use the derivative signs to identify which is the local maximum and which is the local minimum.
hints.recap: For three distinct crossings, a positive-leading cubic must have its local maximum above the axis and its local minimum below the axis.
hints.pitfall: A turning height equal to zero produces a repeated root, so check the strict boundary carefully.
hints.pause: Calculate both heights and write the required sign conditions in terms of the parameters.

recall.reminder: A positive-leading cubic has three distinct real roots exactly when its maximum is positive and its minimum negative.

hints.title: Combine the parameter restrictions
hints.body: Rearrange the sign conditions obtained from your two height expressions into bounds on the requested parameter. Intersect them and check that the resulting interval is nonempty under the given assumptions.
hints.recap: Both turning-height conditions must hold for the same cubic.
hints.pitfall: One height condition alone does not force three distinct real roots.
hints.pause: Derive the complete strict parameter interval and check its boundary cases.

recall.reminder: Combine the turning-height sign requirements and check equality boundaries separately.

solution:
f′(x)=2x(x+2m) vanishes at −2m and 0. The first is a local maximum and the second a local minimum because m>0.

The heights are f(−2m)=n+8m3/3 and f(0)=n. Three distinct roots require n+8m3/3>0 and n<0.

Hence −8m3/3<n<0: A.
knowledgePattern: Cubic extrema must straddle zero for three distinct roots
